doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Seven years on the Dean Martin Show and the theme tenor solo
summary: He recalls the collapsible piano gag and was on the show seven years. He played the prominent tenor solo on the theme, which Les Brown's road tenor was often credited for.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I have this really specific memory, I don’t know if you were on playing the Dean Martin Show. You know he would always come out and jump on the piano, and one time they had a collapsible piano?
Were you on the show then?

I think the show was on ten years, and I was on there seven. And when the staff orchestra ended then I left because I got a chance to do the Carol Burnett Show, which was a better paying show. And as a matter of fact I had a tenor solo on the theme of the Dean Martin show that was very prominent, and was heard throughout the country. And Les Brown

was the bandleader on the show. And then he’d go on the road and they’d ask the tenor player if he was the one that played on the — and he wasn’t. He wasn’t even on the show, you know, if he played that solo. So it got a lot of exposure.
Yeah, it was good, it was nice.
